output.summary: The yield drop looks real: CMM gauge R&R, program and reject criteria did not change. New operators reject at the same rate as experienced ones, and yield fell in week 34 before they ran alone, so H4 is contradicted. Rejects roughly doubled on all six lathes. Several causes are live and confounded: 12-hour shift fatigue (no hour-of-shift data), Corvane hardness spread (rose from September, but the decline started in August), and spindle wear (runout is out of limit only on L3-02 and L3-05, and vibration on L3-02 has risen since July). Evidence is insufficient to commit to one root cause. Reverting shifts or cancelling Corvane now is premature. Performance plans and cutting inspection are harmful. Run the staggered spindle service with Tamsworth trials and hour-of-machining analysis.
